news.title: AI Weekly: Nvidia does deal with Wall Street, China's AI weather forecasts
news.summary:
STORY: From Nvidia's deal with Wall Street giants... to China's AI weather forecasting

This is AI Weekly.

:: AI Weekly

Nvidia has partnered with six major financial institutions to launch compute financing platforms.

They are aimed at raising over $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said on X the company has the option to backstop up to $125 billion, or 25% of the potential deals.

The move highlights how surging demand for AI computing capacity is drawing institutional investors.

South Korea will launch a $3.5 billion semiconductor fund targeting promising chip materials, parts, equipment and fabless companies.

Seoul says it seeks to accelerate plans for new chip manufacturing hubs across the country.

Under the plan, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, suppliers and local governments are expected to invest more than $576 billion in new chip manufacturing projects.

A French press association has asked the country's competition watchdog to take action against Google's AI-generated article summaries.

The trade group says they deprive newspapers and magazines of readers.

The group has called on the regulator to make a decision similar to one ordered against Meta.

To put forward a payment plan and resume talks with traditional media seeking fees for the use of their content by AI tools.

China is emerging as a leading player in the race to improve weather prediction through AI.

Meteorologists used a new generation of AI weather models alongside traditional forecasting systems as they tracked Typhoon Dolphin's path.

Researchers say they can generate forecasts much faster than conventional systems while matching or surpassing them on some measures of accuracy.
